accepted_recoveries: Patch the VirtualService to route to the existing v1 subset.
Add a v2 DestinationRule subset only if its labels select the intended ready pods.
forbidden_actions: Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.
Do not relabel unrelated workloads to satisfy the broken route.
Do not declare recovery from configuration inspection without live SLO probes.
incident.injected_fault: The checkout VirtualService routes to subset v2 while its DestinationRule defines only subset v1, whose labels match the ready checkout pods.
observable_signals: Checkout requests return HTTP 503 through the mesh ingress.
The ingress proxy reports no healthy upstream for checkout subset v2.
Direct requests to ready checkout pods succeed.
preconditions: The mesh control plane and ingress gateway are healthy.
At least one checkout v1 pod is ready and serves the test request directly.
No checkout v2 subset is defined before fault injection.
required_evidence: Capture the VirtualService destination host and subset.
Capture DestinationRule subset definitions and labels.
Capture ready checkout pod labels and a successful direct-pod probe.
Capture a failing ingress probe before recovery.
incident.title: VirtualService subset mismatch

constraints: Capture the VirtualService destination host and subset.
Capture all DestinationRule subset definitions and their labels.
Capture ready checkout pod labels and a successful direct-pod probe.
Capture a failing ingress probe before any recovery.
Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.
Do not relabel unrelated workloads to satisfy the route.
Do not declare recovery from configuration inspection alone; require live ingress SLO probes.
Recovery is established only after 3 consecutive windows with HTTP 5xx rate below 0.001 and p95 latency below 200 ms.

Keep investigation scope limited to proofix-case-01/checkout-gateway routing and its associated mesh configuration unless new evidence contradicts the stated healthy control-plane, gateway, and pod preconditions.
payload.impact: checkout-gateway is unavailable through the service-mesh ingress: checkout requests return HTTP 503 because the VirtualService targets undefined subset v2, while the DestinationRule defines only v1 and ready v1 pods serve direct probes successfully. The evidence bounds the fault to mesh routing configuration for checkout-gateway, not the pods, ingress gateway, or mesh control plane.

payload.rationale: The VirtualService sends checkout traffic to subset v2, but the applicable DestinationRule defines only v1 and both ready checkout pods match version=v1. Patch only the route subset to the existing healthy v1 subset. This preserves the mesh path, does not restart workloads or affect persistent data, and is directly reversible. Because no live ingress or direct-pod probe is present, recovery must not be declared until live probes satisfy the SLO.
payload.rollback_trigger: Rollback immediately if the patch is rejected, changes any route beyond the observed checkout route, causes checkout pod readiness or ingress behavior to worsen, or the ingress route continues failing after the expected mesh propagation interval while v1 endpoints remain healthy.

success_criteria.description: After mesh configuration propagation, capture a successful direct-pod probe and successful checkout ingress probes. For three consecutive measurement windows, ingress HTTP 5xx rate must be strictly below 0.001 and p95 latency strictly below 200 ms; checkout pods must remain ready, and no subset-v1 no-healthy-upstream response may appear.
